Ukraine team about Russian language independent media. Lots of Als and follow ups.

collaborating and partnering with you guys! The put together a full proposal. I'm waiting to get the right POC

extremely well in SE Asia. As an aside, some of my team and I will be in Bangkok in November for APEO
where we will have a YouTube Creators studio of journalists from the US, Korea, Japan, and Indonesia
interviewing key government officials.

Vera

2022 Philippines Election
by the Numbers
We've made significant investments in technology and teams to proactively remove harmful content and disrupt
election interference across our platforms. We started preparing for the 2022 Philippine elections a year in
advance, which allowed us to identify emerging threats, and put systems in place to disrupt abuse of our services.
Below is a summary of our efforts ahead of and during Election Day in the Philippines.
Over
15,000
accounts actioned for violating
our Inauthentic Behavior
policies using automated
detection on accounts in the
Philippines.
Ahead of the Philippines election, our
investigative teams took down about 10,000
accounts for violating Inauthentic Behavior
(IB) policy. They used IB tactics to inflate the
distribution of content that included
election-related posts, including some that
used politics as a spam lure at the time when
people were interested in following these
topics. Based on these and earlier insights, we
were able to automate the detection of these
IB patterns to complement manual
investigations. As a result, we identified
hundreds of IB clusters in the Philippines and
took action against over 15,000 thousand
accounts after expert review to ensure we
don't over-enforce. On average, these spammy
clusters were less than six months old when
we disabled them.
Over

technology identifies as likely to be violating

Hi Vera,
Here are my quick notes about the meeting with Josh Blumenfeld today:

• Josh heads up the Government Affairs Department, which has a small team and we can direct all
global inquiries related to YouTube to him. They want to work with USAID
• He is looking for "trusted flaggers" to be a part of their program. these are groups that understand
local context and language that can identify problematic content that YT or its automated systems
would not necessarily catch. (TO DO: we provided him list of Ukraine media observation groups;
we could prepare a select list of our country programs, that would list the implementing
partner and their local partners -- but we should consider a list of priority countries).
• YouTube provides social media / online literacy training programs for CSOs, primarily in the US. His
big "offers" for us to get back to him are:
• Trainings for our communicators (i.e. LPA and DOCs) on how to effectively use YouTube
• Funding a cohort of YouTube creators and or media outlets that use YouTube in their offerings
for equipping and training up on YouTube. Josh will draft up a short concept for us to look at.
We could make it a co-branded regional program or global program. They want to achieve this
by the end of this calendar year. (TO DO: A possible opportunity might be to latch this on
to the RDMA program for fact checkers in that region, that RDMA is currently
approving; another option might be to do something with creators in Ukraine and the
region. We need to decide this internally).
Let me know if you thinkI left out any essential points.
Best,
J
